SMWJAX

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Fernandina Beach to St. Augustine FL out 20
NM...

* Until 445 PM EDT.

* At 345 PM EDT, a strong thunderstorm was located over Talbot
Island, or 38 nm north of Saint Augustine, moving southeast at 20
knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts to nearly 50 knots.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Small craft could be damaged in briefly higher winds and
suddenly higher waves.

Amelia City, Mayport, Talbot Island, Nassau Sound Approach Buoy 6a,

properties.title: Flood Warning issued July 26 at 3:46PM EDT until July 26 at 6:00PM EDT by NWS Charleston SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is occurring.

* WHERE...Berkeley County in southeastern South Carolina...
Charleston County in southeastern South Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 600 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads remain closed due to flooding. Streams
continue to rise due to excess runoff from earlier rainfall. Expect
many areas of slow moving or standing water. It will take several
hours for all the water from these storms to work through local
drainage systems in urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 344 PM EDT, local law enforcement reported a number of road
closures in Isle of Palms, Mount Pleasant and surrounding areas
from ongoing flooding. Between 3 and 5.5 inches of rain have
fallen in these areas since around 1 PM. Emergency officials are
describing this situation as dangerous and are asking people to
stay off the roadways until conditions improve. The risk for
additional flooding has diminished, but it will take some time
for conditions to improve.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mount Pleasant, Isle Of Palms, Sullivan's Island, Mount Pleasant
Towne Centre, Boone Hall Plantation, Sullivans Island, Seaside
Farms, East Cooper Regional Medical Center and Snowden.
- This includes I-526 between mile markers 29 and 31.
properties.instruction:
Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Report flooding directly to the Charleston National Weather Service
at 1-888-383-2024 or email your reports to nws.charlestonsc@noaa.gov.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued July 26 at 2:29PM EDT until July 26 at 4:00PM EDT by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Urban and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall continues.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Florida, including the following
county, Miami-Dade.

* WHEN...Until 400 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways. Ponding of water in urban or other areas is
occurring or is imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 229 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This will cause urban and small stream
flooding. Up to 2 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Miami, Miami Beach, Coral Gables, Key Biscayne, Surfside,
Virginia Key, North Miami, Miami Shores, North Bay Village,
Port Of Miami, Fisher Island, Downtown Miami, Marlins Park,
Coconut Grove, Bay Harbor Islands and Bal Harbour.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.description:
AQAMSO

* WHAT...Air Quality Advisory due to smoke from wildfires.

Air Quality Index ranging from Moderate to Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups.

* WHERE...All Areas on the Nez Perce Reservation.

* WHEN...Until 10:00 AM PDT Monday July 27.

* IMPACTS...Those who experience health effects from smoke include
children under 18, elders, pregnant women, people with asthma
or have difficulty breathing, diabetes, heart problems or
otherwise compromised health, and people who have high exposure
(those who work, exercise, or spend extensive time outdoors).

outdoor exposure and limit indoor activities, and everyone should
restrict their outdoor activities.
